findings.reason: the missing dependency lets the filter node run against an absent fixture, so its done-when fails for a scheduling reason rather than a code reason.
findings.text: §8 `mapping-class-filter`'s `plan-section-depends-on` lists only `signal-cocos-conventions#s3`, but its node text says it runs "after `signal-cocos-conventions` §3 and §2" and its done-when checks `tests/fixtures/conventions/reference_labels.json`, the fixture that signal-cocos-conventions §2 (`convention-reference-labels`) creates; a scheduler reading the declarations can dispatch §8 before that fixture exists

findings.reason: without the §6 dependency the resolver and slot judgment run before the geometry edge exists and silently carry no sensor geometry, so the orientation context the plan relies on is absent when the §7 proof runs.
findings.text: §4 reads "its HAS_GEOMETRY sensor geometry" from the source and §5's judgment state carries it, but HAS_GEOMETRY is introduced by `signal-cocos-conventions` §6 while §4's `depends-on` lists only that plan's §3

findings.reason: without a control that must fail, the proof cannot distinguish a working chain from one whose Jev/local-settled signs were never exercised.
findings.text: the §7 proof node's done-when asserts "no written binding's sign disagrees with its source's recorded convention" and names no negative control; for the code-settled majority the written sign is produced by the same `cocos_sign` the comparison invokes, and a none-class source has no recorded convention to compare
